toegepas.voor: te praat soos daardie karakter sou
toegepas.na: te praat soos daardie karakter sou doen
toegepas.rede_vinder: Ending on a bare 'sou' copies English 'as that character would'; Afrikaans needs a verb after the modal, and 'doen' covers both verbs.
toegepas.fout: The definition ends on a bare modal 'sou', copying English 'as that character would', and leaves out the verb Afrikaans needs.
toegepas.rede_keurder: Adding the missing verb 'doen' is a grammar fix that does not change the meaning, and this definition is not one of the shared ones.

laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'Kom kyk daarna' is the natural Afrikaans for going to watch a performance; 'kom dit sien' reads stiffly.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'Besoekers kom dit sien' is ordinary, acceptable Afrikaans, and 'kyk daarna' can also be read as 'look after it', so the proposal is a lateral move that adds an ambiguity.

laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'sy' can be read as 'she' or 'his' and is unclear here; 'n beeld' gives the same image without the unclear pronoun.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: Before a noun 'sy' can only be the possessive and clearly points to the partner, and swapping it for 'n beeld' drops whose reflection you are.

na_skrywer.rede_vinder: 'n dans dans' repeats the same word as noun and verb and reads clumsily; 'uitvoer' keeps the meaning.
na_skrywer.fout: 'n dans dans' repeats the same word as noun and verb and reads slightly clumsily in a glossary definition.
na_skrywer.rede_keurder: This is a glossary definition, and 'uitvoer' narrows the meaning to performing for an audience, which leaves out dancing to celebrate together, so the writer should find another fix.
na_skrywer.waarom: the reviewer sent it to the writer

vlae.teks: Hulle strek hulle arms, bene en rug na bo.
vlae.rede: 'Strek hulle bene en rug na bo' is an unusual way to put it, and legs are not always stretched upward; a clearer wording would mean guessing what is intended, so this is for the writer.

beskerm_bedenkings.rede: Under AWS 2017 a compound built on a hyphenated part is joined with a hyphen ('C-majeur-toonaard'), and the definition itself writes 'majeur-toonaard'; the open spelling in the headword looks inconsistent. This needs a person's decision, because the term is shared with lesson 4.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: Langs mekaar wys die drie punte hoe verskillend die twee danse is.
laat_vaar_vorige.na: Die drie punte wys hoe verskillend die twee danse langs mekaar is.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: As written, 'langs mekaar' attaches to the three points rather than the two dances; the reorder fixes the reference without adding words.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: The fronted 'Langs mekaar' reads naturally and echoes the heading; the reorder is a lateral move that now suggests the dances stand physically side by side.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: Dit is die klem en nie die enigste
laat_vaar_vorige.na: Dit is die klem, nie die enigste
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'en nie' makes the contrast read like an addition; a comma states the contrast directly and saves a word.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'Dit is die klem en nie die enigste ...' is ordinary natural Afrikaans; the comma version is only different.

laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'Opgemaakte' echoes English 'made-up'; 'versinde' is the standard Afrikaans word.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'Opgemaakte' is established, plain Afrikaans (as in 'n opgemaakte storie'), while 'versinde' is harder for a Grade 5 reader and rewords a glossary definition for no clear gain.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: Die dans is na daardie stewels genoem
laat_vaar_vorige.na: Die dans is na daardie stewels vernoem
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'Na iets genoem' calques English 'named after'; the Afrikaans idiom is 'na iets vernoem'.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'Na iets genoem' is ordinary, correct Afrikaans (as in 'n kind na sy oupa noem), not a calque, so 'vernoem' is a lateral swap.

laat_vaar_vorige.blok: Gumboot-dans: hoe dit lyk en klink
laat_vaar_vorige.voor: volg die span dikwels die maat
laat_vaar_vorige.na: volg die span dikwels die ritme
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'Die maat volg' can be read as 'follow the partner', since the glossary uses 'maat' for a partner; 'ritme' is the lesson's own word for the beat and keeps the meaning.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'Die maat volg' is the fixed musical expression for keeping time to the musicians' beat, and changing it to 'ritme' swaps a term of art and moves the meaning in a lesson that sets the dancers' own rhythm against the music.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: Dit is die klem en nie
laat_vaar_vorige.na: Dit is elke dans se klem en nie
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: The bare 'Dit' has no clear referent after two sentences about two dances; naming whose emphasis it is makes the reference clear without adding content.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: In context 'Dit is die klem' clearly refers to the two contrasts just named, and 'elke dans se klem' can be misread as a claim about every dance in general.
